utterances.text: Well, it is not possible for that to be completed today, but I'm sure that the lawyers are not unmindful of your personal situation and that when we return to complete your testimony next week, that they will expedite matters to -- so that you can return to your ordinary affairs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, could I have it marked for identification. It wasn't on our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P101 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And we'll now take a break for them to assemble the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The next witness for the Prosecution is ST-13. He has protective measures which were granted sometime ago and they are facial/voice distortion, and pseudonym. He is -- while he is currently being brought over, sirs, he was a Muslim reserve policeman in Kotor Varos at the relevant time and is survivor of the killings outside the Kotor Varos hospital in June 1992 that forms the basis of his prior testimony and statement which will be admitted through 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: While we wait for the witness to be brought in, I have noticed that we are facing, and increasingly so, a problem of timing, and I would like to suggest that sometime maybe next week or the week thereafter, we sit down in a 65 ter context with the parties and try to agree on a plan for the next couple of months as to which witnesses we will have time to hear and when and for how long and so on. So if the parties are ready to meet up with the Judges and the senior legal officer, of course, for the purposes of planning for the next months, I would be grateful. And in accordance with this, I would like the Prosecution to draw up a list of its witnesses for the next eight weeks. You can decide when, but if you can put up the list by sometime next week, then we will take a meeting soon thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, we can accommodate that, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir, and thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give your testimony. For the purpose of just establishing your identity, I would like to ask the Registrar to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. What is going to happen now is that the Prosecution will examine you first, and since you are being examined here under an expedited procedure, the Prosecution will have only roughly 20 minutes, perhaps 30 minutes to go through your earlier testimony and your statements, which we have all read. So the Court is fully aware of what you have earlier indicated to the Prosecution's investigators. And after that, you will be cross-examined on the basis of your statements, first by the counsel for Mico Stanisic, which is counsel Zecevic. And I believe that Mr. Zecevic has asked for 30 minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: To complete his cross-examination. And thereafter you will be cross-examined, finally, by counsel Krgovic, who has asked for, was it 40 minutes or 45 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: 30 minutes would be enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thirty minutes. Another 30 minutes by Mr. Krgovic. And after that your testimony is completed, and you will be able to return to your home after that. So if you have no other questions to put, I suggest we get on with it. Do you have anything that you wish to clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very good. The witness is yours, Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I think we need to tender the pseudonym sheet formally, if I could that under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P102 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall making a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 15th and 16th of August, 2000?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And have you been given the opportunity to read this statement in the past few days?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you confirm today that the contents of that statement are true and correct to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If I could tender the statement, please, it's 65 ter 10015 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Tendered, admitted, and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P103 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall reading that statement and making some minor changes before you testified in the Brdjanin trial in 2003?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, as you have requested the proofing notes from the proofing for this trial, I considered it prudent to add to the proofing note from the previous trial which simply were some minor changes to the statement before he testified, so you have the complete background of this witness's prior testimony. So even though this proofing note was not in the formal 92 ter package, we didn't include any proofing notes because we didn't think Your Honours would require them. But because you have requested these ones, I thought it prudent to add this one in as well, it was disclosed long ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pidwell, we will allow it to be admitted in the 65 ter list and included in the statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That is 65 ter 10017. I seek to admit that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P103.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall coming to the Tribunal and giving evidence in the trial against Brdjanin one day on the 20th of June, 2003?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And have you been given the opportunity over the past few days to listen to the audiotape of that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And if I asked you the same questions that were put to you in that trial, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I seek to admit the transcript of the prior testimony, 10014 -- sorry, 65 ter number 10014. That's testimony on the 20th of June, 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P103.2, Your Honours. Under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And there are two proofing notes in relation to this witness that I'd also like to tender. 65 ter 10016 and 65 ter 10018.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P103.3, Your Honours. All will be under seal as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, there were five documents which were in this witness's 92 ter package. A map, a certificate, and three photos. These were not previously on the Prosecutor's 65 ter list but were noted in the package as being relevant to understanding the testimony of this witness, but in accordance with Your Honours' rulings, as the Prosecution interpreted it, of 2 October we now seek to tender these as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, could you inform us what these documents are?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And perhaps show them to us because we have this hesitance, you know, of admitting stuff that we don't know what is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Certainly sir, we can bring them up for you. It's a map of the town which is, when you read the testimony, is -- he refers to it. And so that was why it was associated, so that when you are reading the testimony you actually can follow with the document that he is referring to. Same with -- there's three photos as well. So when he is led through his testimony in the trial, he is shown these photographs and describes certain things. And it was the Prosecution's view that without actually having the document there, it would be difficult to follow the transcript. They weren't previously on the 65 ter list because we had taken the position that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand that they were not. But I did not come across those photos when I read the statement, so I haven't seen them. I would like to see them before we admit them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So 65 ter 3425 is the map that's referred to. If that could be brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this will enable us to appreciate the testimony and the statements -- the evidence, sorry, the evidence in the statement. So unless the Defence has any objections, we would be ready to admit it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If that could be admitted as Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P103.4, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter 3426, and we may have to go into private session in order to view this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can assist the Tribunal. This is a photograph of the Kotor Varos hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P103.6, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you. The next one is 65 ter 3428. It's another photograph of a different view of the Kotor Varos hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And this is?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: This is part of the hospital grounds and in his prior testimony, he refers to it, in particular the tree. It may assist you when you are reading the transcript through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P103.8 [sic], Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 7, no?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: .7. I apologise, Your Honours. You are right, it's .7.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And the last one is -- finally, one more photograph, 65 ter 3429, and this is the field behind the hospital when it comes up. It's the field behind the hospital. And once again it will assist Your Honours when reading the testimony to give some context to where the hospital was and the layout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P103.8.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, I just have a few questions for you now. You were a reserve policeman in Kotor Varos from 1979 until the end of 1991. Could you please explain for the Trial Chamber the role of a reserve policeman at that time?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: At that time after completing my compulsory military service in the JNA, all the young men and other citizens had their assignments. I was assigned to reserve police. Our task was to join active duty police in patrolling the town, to secure socially-owned or other significant facilities in the municipality of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And during the time of that, when you were first given the role of a reserve policeman in 1979 and up until the end of 1991, do you recall how many times you were in fact deployed in that role?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Twice. One time it was when the Yugoslav president, Josip Broz Tito died -- or actually before he died, while he was ill; and the second time was during the winter Olympic games.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And in your statement you say that you were ordered to work for the Kotor Varos police at the end of -- or in December 1991. Can you advise the Trial Chamber who ordered you to work as a policeman at that time?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: We received our orders from the chief of police, or rather the commander of the police. Savo Tepic was the chief of police at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, how were you told that you were now required to work full time for the Kotor Varos police?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: The Kotor Varos receive [as interpreted] police members received papers calling us up to report at the police station in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I wonder if a correction needs to be made to the transcript or if the translation was wrong. The page 56 line 2, it says the Kotor Varos "receive" police members. I think it's supposed to read reserve police members.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: When you were ordered to come and work for the Kotor Varos police at this time, were you issued with a uniform?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I had my uniform from before since 1979.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And can you just describe that uniform, please.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I had a winter uniform, colour blue, dark blue. I also had a shirt and a tie.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Was the material used for this uniform camouflage or non-camouflage?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Non-camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And were you issued with a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I was issued a piece of weapon in December 1979.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And what kind of weapon was that?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you've told us that from 1979 until 1991, you were only required to form your reserve police duties on two occasions. The rest of the time where was your rifle kit, the rifle that you were issued from the police?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I didn't have a rifle since 1979. I received the rifle in December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Right. So from December 1991, where was the rifle kept when you were off duty?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I kept it at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you describe a uniform with a flower on it, the translation is a snowdrop. Which uniform had a white flower on it?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Olive drab military uniforms had it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you know which military or police formation wore these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: They were worn by the members of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And just on that note, where was the -- do you know where the Territorial Defence offices were in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: The police offices were at the new police station, and on the floor above in the same building were the offices of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm just going to show you some photos in a minute, but just to clarify the issue of your weapon, when you say that you kept your rifle at home, was that -- was that the practice of the Kotor Varos police? Were you in fact allowed to do that, or was it something that you just did of your own accord?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: We were allowed to take our rifles home at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Can I please have 65 ter 3417, please. Your Honours, this is a -- this is a compilation of maps and photos which the Prosecution has put together to try and assist the Trial Chamber with the witness in giving some perspective to the areas that we're talking about. This is the first time we are going use it, and the technical side of it may elude me, slightly. It's in sanction, which means I think we control that, rather than the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, you'll see on your computer screen there a photograph. Do you recognise that town?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And can you describe -- do you know the name of the street that is the main street that we see on the right-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the street, but it leads from Banja Luka towards Teslic via Vrbanjci, but I honestly don't know its name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: In your statement you talk about being taken over a bridge. Do you see the bridge in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I think I might ask the witness to draw on the photograph, and I think I'm going to have to bring it up in e-court. 65 ter 10120.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I don't know what kind of implement shall I use to do the marking?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: The Court Officer will assist you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you able to -- sir, with that -- the pen in your hand, you are able to mark, to draw where you see the bridge. Are you able to do that?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I'm taking instructions on the technical side of this. If we could note that 1 is the bridge that the witness is referring to so that we can have an understanding between the transcript and the exhibit. The witness needs to mark --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If you could mark, sir, the bridge at number 1 so we can follow the testimony, please.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you see the sawmill in Kotor Varos in that picture?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: This is the direction towards Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness is unintelligible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sawmill is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Could you mark that with a number 2, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you see the Catholic church on that picture?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Would you mark that with number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you see the Kotor Varos hospital on that picture?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Could you mark that with number 4, please.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you know where the SJB building is in Kotor Varos from that picture?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And could you mark that number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It's not that clear from the photograph, so perhaps you could assist us. The area between your number 4 and number 5, we see there's an empty area without any buildings; what is that?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: This is a football stadium. This is a school and -- an elementary school, a gym, a secondary school, and these are the workshops where I underwent training to be a blacksmith, and these are the garages. This is the entrance from the main street to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you know if that football stadium is a standard size football stadium?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes. It was of a standard size except for the stands, because there wasn't enough space at the time. Today it's bigger. But the size of the pitch itself is standard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, shouldn't you ask the witness to indicate where the football stadium is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Could you mark the football stadium on there as well and mark it with the number 6, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know where the municipal building is in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: The municipal assembly is in the direction of Vrbanjci, but you cannot see it on this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know how far it was from the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Approximately another distance equal to the one that we see now in the direction of Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know how far it was -- or it is, was, from the SJB building to the Catholic church?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Well, approximately or maybe even more than the distance between the hospital and the Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you able to give us an estimate of the kilometre or metre range?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: If you take a paved road between 300 and 400 metres, or 500 maximum, if you walk this way. But I don't believe that the distance is that long, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know where Savo Tepic lived in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: He had an apartment at Bregovi, just behind the church in these buildings here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Could you mark on the photo, please, where that is and mark it with number 7.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know where Nedjelko Djekanovic lived in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Probably in the same area, at Bregovi, since in that area all of the apartments were state-owned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, we are coming to the break. We have to take the break at 5 minutes past, so if you could round up and be ready by then, then we can take the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm in fact finished with this witness, sir. I was going to seek to tender that; I think I have to tender it separately now that it's marked, as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Accepted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P104, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now take the break, and we will adjourn in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know I indicated I had finished with the witness, I have one question if I may be permitted to ask it? Sorry, Your Honours. I'll repeat. I had indicated I'd finished with this witness, but I do have one further question if I'm permitted to ask it. It is just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I am afraid, Ms. Pidwell, that if we are to finish this witness today, that won't be possible. We have indications by the Defence that they need approximately one half-hour, and that's already -- we don't even have time for that. So I suggest that if we can conclude the cross-examinations and there still is a couple of minutes left before we adjourn today, then you can put your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic and also Mr. Krgovic, I kindly ask you to see if it is possible to conclude the cross-examination of this witness before we have to adjourn today. The witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure we will be able it to accommodate the Trial Chamber and the witness. But, just Your Honours, I mean, if Ms. Pidwell wants to ask the question, maybe it's better that she ask now because after that, we might have a issue with that and we will need to re-cross examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's very well. I agree with you. But she's taking off time from you and Mr. Krgovic -- are you allowed to give her that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well, Ms. Pidwell, quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, did you know a Muslim police officer by the name of Zahirovic?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: A Muslim by the name of Zahirovic? He may have been a reserve policeman, but I don't know of such an active duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: That was my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, as we speak the same language, you will probably wish to answer as quickly as possible, but please wait a moment since I need to turn the -- my microphone off first for the sake of the protective measures. So please keep that in mind. You told us that as of 1979, you had a uniform since you were with the reserve police; correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All other reserve policemen as far as you know, had their uniforms at home as of the moment becoming a member of the reserve force or be it the police or army?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So all reservists whether policemen or soldiers had their respective uniforms at home; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were issued with weapons only when called up from reserve to tend to a particular task; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said that as of 1979 until 1991, on two occasions when the late President Tito was sick, and during the Olympics in Sarajevo, you were called up from the reserve force. Were you then issued with any weapons?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes, but we didn't take the weapons home during those periods of time; we only had them while we were on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, as the reserve policemen you were called up from the reserve force, issued with a piece of weapon, and while on duty you had that weapon, once you would go home, you would leave the piece in the station and once again on duty, you would take the weapon again; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this case in 1991, you had an additional, let's call it, benefit, an additional courtesy because you were allowed to take your weapons home?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I see in the transcript of your interview or discussions with the OTP dated two days ago that you said, as we were notified by the OTP, that you were invited to give an oath or a declaration by the MUP and that you obeyed.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: When one is issued with weapons, one needs to declare that he or she is going to use it only for the needs of the service and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you are a reserve policeman, you are called up for duty, on which occasion you were issued with a piece of weapon. But before receiving the weapon, you give a solemn declaration, is that so?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether you make the solemn declaration because at the moment of being issued with a weapon, you are being accorded the status of an authorise official, are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes, as a reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I read out the text of the solemn declaration to you, do you think you would be able to recall it, or do you want me to show it to you on the screen, that legal text of the declaration?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: You can show it to me, but we gave declarations and made oaths in the army and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter 1 Article 42 in e-court. Forty-two.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt, but we don't seem to have received any notification of the documents that you are going to use in cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I just tried before -- before this session to notify you that I found in your proofing notes which we received yesterday only that this issue pops up. If you don't -- if you are objecting to it, I can read the solemn declaration. I just wanted to accommodate the witness, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If this is the only document, I don't have any objection, but in accordance with Your Honours' practice or directions, that if there are a number of documents I'd appreciate notification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is definitely the only document, and the only reason is that I want to accommodate the witness. Thank you. Can we have it? [Interpretation] Thank you. You should leave it like this. I confused the numbers, I believe. It is Article 41 actually that contains the solemn declaration. "I declare that I will perform the duties of an authorised official conscientiously and responsibly. That I will abide by the constitution and the law, and that -- could you please just leave the document. We are having a problem, I'm reading from the document. I told you that it was perfect how it was at the very beginning. I need the last paragraph of 41. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat, I apologise. "I declare that I will perform the duties of an authorised official conscientiously and responsibly, that I will abide by the constitution and the law, and that I will protect with all my power the constitutionally-determined system, the rights, freedoms, and safety of working people and citizens, and that I will perform these and other jobs and tasks of an authorised official even in the cases when their execution may put my life in danger." Is this the text of the solemn declaration you made?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I didn't make it, I received a solemn declaration binding me to follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this the solemn declaration as I read it out to you?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Well, this is in Cyrillic, and probably at that time when I had given it, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the document I'm showing you is the law on the interior of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia Herzegovina from 1990. As for it being in the Cyrillic script, you know yourself that the Official Gazettes in Bosnia-Herzegovina were printed in turn, one volume would be in the Latin script and the other in the Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: No, we were using the Latin script.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, let's not dwell on this, it is not in dispute, and we have the document in e-court as Prosecution evidence. Can you recall the text of the solemn declaration or not?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes, the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you make that declaration in December 1991 when you were issued with weapons in the public security station in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Since we were issued with weapons, we had to make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But that was in December 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you. [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to approach the microphone. We are having difficulties hearing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On behalf of Mr. Zupljanin's Defence I will put questions to you in relation to the statement you made in the Brdjanin case. Sir, did you at some point in time during 1992 sign another statement similar to this one when there were certain changes within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After the signing of that statement there were no significant changes to your duties until the conflict broke out in June 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You continued performing your tasks the way you had before signing the statement?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, in the Brdjanin case, you described in detail the events in the health centre. I won't go into any detail, I just wanted to clear up certain names with you and that will be the gist of my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since there is a possibility when discussing these names that the witness's identity be put in danger or easily discovered, hence I would kindly ask that we go into private session so as to protect his identity from the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, before you appeared in court today you had a conversation with the Prosecutor and you mentioned that you had heard from someone that Stojan Zupljanin may have been in Kotor Varos in 1992 in the month of June.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You couldn't tell us who told you about this, and we understand that in view of the time that has elapsed. And it's understandable that you couldn't provide more details on this; correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: That's correct, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Krgovic. Any redirect from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked some questions about a solemn declaration first of all by Mr. Zecevic, and then later on about -- that you signed another statement by Mr. Krgovic. The second statement that you signed, do you recall what that was about or why you were required to sign that one?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Well, these declarations or statements were almost identical in their wording. This was just to once again confirm that the weapons that we had on us at home, that we were not going to use them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you know why you were required to sign the oath or this statement again, or make this declaration again?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I don't know. The purpose was probably the same as in the case the first instance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: You were also asked some questions about the identity of the people who were committing the crimes outside the hospital, and I think the term used was "locals." Were there any men there that you saw involved in these crimes who were not locals?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: I understood the question to refer to just the names that were mentioned, the persons mentioned, but the other individuals were the so-called specials.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And when you use the term "specials," could you clarify what you mean, please.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: These were specially trained units with uniforms and caps on their heads.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's request: Could the witness repeat the last portion. He was not intelligible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer, the interpreters didn't quite catch it. So the question was when you used the term "specials," could you clarify what you mean, and the interpreters have written, these are specially trained units with uniforms and caps on their heads. Was there anything else you wanted to add?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Well, they had hats on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can help. He mentioned -- [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wanted to assist because I did hear the witness and I was trying to help the witness. Perhaps the witness can take off his head set if you have a problem with this question, but I heard the witness to say SOS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] SOS, no. Special units.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It's just that this practice, sir, is of concern to the Prosecution, the intervention of the Defence counsel when there is an issue with translation, we don't have the benefit of the two languages. And in my submission, it's not appropriate for the Defence lawyers to step in, even if they are thinking they are assisting, to intervene in the evidence that is coming through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I realise that this may be a problem that occurs frequently. If the Defence counsels have questions about the interpretation, I suggest that you raise the matter, I think you should, but please don't try to reformulate what you think the witness said. It's better just to say that there is a problem and have the witness repeat what he said. Thanks. Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Just finally, so we can clarify this point, your answer said the special units had hats on and then there was some -- we required some clarification on that. Could you describe the hats of the specials, please.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: They had hats on, they looked like cowboy hats, and they had camouflage green hats.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you've referred in your statement to someone who was mentioned by the name of Dubocanin. Can you describe the uniform that he wore.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: Slobodan Dubocanin had a camouflage uniform on and a hat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have a problem here. I never mentioned Mr. Dubocanin, that's number 1; and two, the witness never at any point in his testimony mentions Slobodan Dubocanin being outside the health centre. So I think that this was ever mentioned in the cross-examination, nor does it arise from the transcript of the witness as far as the events outside the health centre are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, can you clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, Slobodan Dubocanin's name is mentioned in the witness's testimony. He was then asked about specific names of perpetrators outside of the killing -- of the killings outside the hospital. And my learned friend did not mention Slobodan Dubocanin, and I am trying to show that by omission, he has -- he did not say the name deliberately, and if the transcript is read in conjunction with the cross-examination, you'll see that what the Prosecution is trying to show is that this man was there. But the line of testimony showed that he excluded the name and was trying to make it a finite group of men who were there at the time. I'm sorry, it sounds a little bit confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It is, actually. I still don't know if the name was mentioned or not during the cross-examination, but obviously if it was not, then that's beyond the scope of your redirect.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Let's leave it at that, sir, and I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, when you tell us about special unit, in your view, were they military or were they police?

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: They had army uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I would have had the same question. So just to be completely sure that I understood your answer correctly, do you know if the specials were under the command of the army or under the command of the police? That is to say, regardless of what kind of uniforms they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: ST-13
utterances.text: While I was in prison, we were told that the police could not save us because we were held prisoner by the army. However, the uniforms, the camouflage drab grey uniforms were army uniforms, or army reserve uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. If no other questions are to be put to this witness, I would like to thank you very much again for coming to The Hague to give your testimony, and what you have offered during your testimony here will be included in the files of this trial and in the judgement in the end. I wish you a safe trip back to your home country or to the place where you reside, and you are now being excused and released. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, there's just one procedural matter that the case manager has just brought to my attention which I understand has to be dealt with now. There was a portion of time when my learned friend was standing up addressing the Court when his microphone was on and the witness's voice would have been transmitted without the distortion. And that piece needs to be redacted, and I understand I need to make a formal application now for that occur within five minutes of it occurring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, can this be done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, again, Mr. Witness, you may now leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May I just raise something in relation to the last matter. The complaint that Ms. Pidwell was making was one which I think we ought to clear up. Certain limited parts of the transcript were quoted from the Brdjanin case by Mr. Krgovic. He omitted the large number of references it to Slobodan Dubocanin's presence and indeed interrogation that this witness that also litter the transcript. If a misleading impression is given in that way, either counsel can stand up and ask Defence counsel to deal with the other parts of the transcript that mention all over the place Mr. Dubocanin, or alternatively wait to deal with it in re-examination. So to that extent that was what the purpose of Ms. Pidwell's questioning about Dubocanin was. But if Your Honours -- I know Your Honours got a copy of the transcript, you will see indeed there's a whole reference that actually came out in cross-examination to Slobodan Dubocanin actually interrogating this witness, and also being the one that was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. I must admit, I mean, I was perfectly aware of Mr. Dubocanin's name being mentioned, but it skipped me that the parts that were referred to by Mr. Krgovic were those parts in which his name --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: His name isn't mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And so --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my cross-examination was related directly to the events outside the health centre. In the evidence given in the Brdjanin case, the witness never mentioned the presence of Mr. Dubocanin outside the health centre. And since my cross-examination pertained exclusively to this incident, there is no doubt that if the Prosecutor claims that this person was indeed mentioned in this incident, let us please have either the page number or any other reference, and that was the essence of my objection granted by the Chamber. I asked this witness about specific persons whose name were given, and the people who he recognised as the perpetrators of the crime. However, neither in the Brdjanin case, nor in his statement that was admitted into evidence there is no mention of Mr. Dubocanin. He did mention him in the events preceding this one, but he is not highlighted here as the person who was in charge or commanded these men who committed these crimes. And that was the essence of my objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours have the transcript. I'm not going to take this further and waste time, but that -- just so that the explanation as to how this came about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. I think we can leave it at that, if that's fine with you. We still have another 12 minutes, and I suppose it doesn't make sense to call back Mr. Djekanovic for 12 minutes cross-examination. Are there any other procedural matters that we should deal with? Sorry, Judge Delvoie has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't have a question. I would still like to inform the parties about the extended sitting in compensation of the 16th of October. We will sit on the 19th to 20th and the 21st of October as scheduled in the morning, and an extended sitting from 1445 to 1615. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And we have Thursday -- the same extended sitting on Thursday in reserve.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, can I ask what that means, because obviously we are lining up witnesses. You mean, if somebody -- a witness runs over? All right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: As you will see in the court calendar, Thursday has been reserved with the same extended times, so if by any chance we need it, we can have it. Otherwise we will just stick to what is originally foreseen in the extended hearings for Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. That will be very helpful. In fact, I think we will need the extended sitting on Thursday as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We have to compensate four hours of the 16th, and we can do that normally in three days, so the Thursday is extra.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to mention one thing which we were notified by our clients. This extended sitting, we understand the reason, and of course we have to make up for the time which is lost for one of the days. But that extended sitting in court, in fact, causes enormous problems for the accused. In a sense that if they have extended sitting, they are deprived of a walk outside in these days and some other -- there are some other issues, which I'm not prepared, I just wanted to put the Trial Chamber on notice. So we might want to discuss that during the 65 ter conference which you suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. Thanks, and I appreciate your bringing this to our attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just also clarify one thing because we are, I think, also slightly confused. In the light of Your Honours' ruling about the admission of 92 ter statements and documents, the last one, the one before this we simply handed in the statement with the accompanying documents, and they were numbered by the court clerk. In order to save time so that -- because obviously we are all anxious to save as much time as possible. And I don't know how I have the nerve to say that, but nonetheless I'm saying it. Would it be possible for the case manager, Mr. Smith, to send to the Registry the list and then pre-number them, so we only take about one minute or something to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is a matter that we should discuss at the 65 ter conference when we get together at that occasion. Our legal officer has suggested that if the Prosecution sends us the -- a list of attached documents in advance, and also sends that list to the Registrar, then the Registrar might pre-number these additional exhibits so that even before we enter into courtroom, we know what they are and what numbers will be given to them, provided they are admitted. That may be one way of going about it, but I suggest that we take it up at the 65 ter conference. Anything else? I give the floor back to the presiding judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. We take the adjournment now, and we resume in Courtroom II on Monday morning at 9 a.m. And I trust that everyone has a safe and enjoyable weekend.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honour, we looked at it, and we thought that it was Courtroom I because of the videolink. Maybe I'm wrong. I mean, I'm not sure how we can do a videolink in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We are scheduled in Courtroom II. We'll see what happens on Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of October, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
